title: Staff record a purchase in the form and it is saved as PENDING with the right total, without touching stock or ledger
why_it_matters: A purchase is a draft until the owner approves it; if saving alone moved stock or the supplier balance, every unapproved draft would distort the books.
steps:
1. Setup: two SMALL_BALES items A and B for 'Ironwood Imports' via POST /api/items. Record their on-hand stock and the 'Ironwood Imports' ledger balance and entry count. Open /purchase/create as ADMIN.
2. Select company 'Ironwood Imports' and List Type SMALL_BALES
3. Keep only A and B; Edit All; A: 3 bales × Rs 10/bale, B: 2 bales × Rs 20/bale; type the rates over the defaults; Save All
4. Enter a unique Invoice No and Sur Charge 50
5. Click 'Create Purchase'
6. Reload; GET /api/purchase/{id}
7. GET /api/inventory and the company ledger
8. Create a second purchase the same way with one line (A: 2 bales × Rs 10/bale), Invoice No empty and Sur Charge 0; reload; GET
expected:
1. Heading 'Create Purchase Order'; Total Amount and Total Bundle(s) show 0; 'Create Purchase' is disabled
2. 'Rate Per Bale' column; only that company's SMALL_BALES items are listed, including A and B
3. Total Bundle(s) = 5; Total Amount = 70
4. Total Amount = 120
5. Redirected to /purchase; new row shows Ironwood Imports, SMALL_BALES, the invoice, Sur Charge 50, total 120, PENDING
6. totalAmount 120, surCharge 50, exactly the 2 lines with the typed bales and rates; status PENDING
7. Stock, balance and entry count unchanged
8. No error toast; PENDING; invoiceNumber null ('N/A' in the list); totalAmount 20

title: Every pricing method gives the same total on screen, in the saved purchase and in the supplier ledger
why_it_matters: The purchase total becomes what the business owes the supplier; a wrong multiplier means paying the wrong amount.
steps: 1. For each row, create the purchase in the UI, check the on-screen total, create, reload and GET, then approve via the API and GET the company ledger. Use multiple bales so a missing bale multiplier can't pass.
expected: 1. On-screen Total Amount, saved totalAmount and the single new ledger DEBIT all equal the expected total; balance rises by exactly that amount
data:
Row | Company / type | Lines | Sur Charge | Expected total = saved total = ledger DEBIT
kg | 'Ironwood Garments' BIG_BALES | 3 bales × 50 kg × Rs 100/kg | 0 | 15,000
lb | 'Ironwood Garments' BIG_BALES | 2 bales × 100 lb × Rs 40/lb | 0 | 8,000
per bale | 'Ironwood Imports' SMALL_BALES | 3 bales × Rs 10/bale, 2 bales × Rs 20/bale | 0 | 70
mixed, decimals | 'Ironwood Garments' BIG_BALES | 4 bales × 12.5 kg × Rs 10.4/kg, 2 bales × 100 lb × Rs 40/lb | 75 | 8,595 (surcharge added once; decimals saved)
notes: The kg, lb and mixed rows are expected to fail (weight-pricing bug). Keep them in a separate `test.fixme()` test from the per-bale row.
known_issue: Kg, lb and mixed rows expected to fail (weight pricing)

expected:

expected: 1. Each row gives its expected result.

Row | Request | Expected
empty product list | purchasedProducts [] | 4xx
negative values | noOfBales -1, baleWeightKgs -10, ratePerKgs -5, surCharge -50, one at a time | 400

title: An approval posts exactly once, whether sent twice at the same time or retried after a lost response
why_it_matters: The owner approves in batches, double-clicks and retries on slow connections; a second posting doubles the stock and the debt.
steps:
1. PENDING P1: 5 bales (500); record S, B. Approve from two ADMIN contexts in parallel (API)
2. PENDING P2: 5 bales (500); record S, B. Approve from the list with a route that forwards the request (route.fetch) and then aborts the response
3. Reload; approve P2 again
4. GET inventory and ledger
expected:
1. One 200, one 'already approved'; stock S + 5; one entry; balance B + 500
2. UI shows failure or no update
3. Refused as already approved, or shows APPROVED
4. S + 5; one entry for P2; B + 500

title: Approving two purchases for the same supplier and item at the same time keeps both postings
why_it_matters: A lost update loses real stock and real debt without any error.
steps: 1. Two PENDING purchases of X: 5 bales (500), 3 bales (300); record S, B. Approve both in parallel
expected: 1. 200 each; X = S + 8; two entries; B + 800; every running balance = previous ± amount
notes: The stored balances can overlap only when both approvals read the balance before either commits, so the test may pass on some runs. Run it with `--repeat-each` before trusting a pass.

title: Running balances stay correct when a purchase is backdated or revised before later purchases and payments
why_it_matters: The supplier statement is read line by line; one wrong running balance makes every later line wrong.
steps:
1. Company with entries dated today; record their running balances, B, and another supplier's balance. Approve a purchase P dated 5 days ago (500)
2. Approve Q dated today (400); record T_Q and B
3. Record a supplier payment of 300 dated today, after Q, via the ledger payment API (confirm the payload against the ledger API and its tests); record its running balance T_pay
4. Revise P to a total 300 higher; approve
5. Revise P to a total 400 lower than step 4; approve
expected:
1. DEBIT 500 ordered before the later entries; each later running balance + 500; balance B + 500; every running balance = previous ± amount; other supplier unchanged
2. Q's running balance = previous + 400
3. Payment row present; balance B - 300
4. P's entry +300; Q T_Q + 300; payment still 300 with T_pay + 300; no new entries; every running balance = previous ± amount
5. Q and payment running balances each drop by 400; final balance = previous final balance - 400
notes:
"Running balance" means the Balance column the supplier statement shows: each row's `partyBalance` from GET /api/ledger/{companyId}?type=company (the stored balance), not the recomputed `runningBalance` field.
Step 1 assumes the statement follows date order. Today rows are listed in entry order and a new backdated purchase doesn't shift later rows (D10). Keep step 1 in its own `test.step` so steps 2–5 still report. If the owner chooses entry order, rewrite step 1.
known_issue: Step 1 expected to fail (D10, ordering pending owner decision)
